claim: SNPC-1.3 is a male germline-enriched variant of a conserved subunit of the small nuclear RNA-activating protein complex.
source: Here we identify SNPC-1.3, a male germline-enriched variant of a conserved subunit of the small nuclear RNA-activating protein complex, as a male-specific piRNA transcription factor in Caenorhabditis elegans.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: SNPC-1.3 is a male-specific piRNA transcription factor in C. elegans.
source: Here we identify SNPC-1.3, a male germline-enriched variant of a conserved subunit of the small nuclear RNA-activating protein complex, as a male-specific piRNA transcription factor in Caenorhabditis elegans.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract.

claim: SNPC-1.3 colocalizes with SNPC-4 in nuclear foci of the male germline.
source: SNPC-1.3 colocalizes with the core piRNA transcription factor, SNPC-4, in nuclear foci of the male germline.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Binding of SNPC-1.3 at male piRNA loci drives spermatogenic piRNA transcription.
source: Binding of SNPC-1.3 at male piRNA loci drives spermatogenic piRNA transcription and requires SNPC-4.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 4.

claim: SNPC-1.3 binding at male piRNA loci requires SNPC-4.
source: Binding of SNPC-1.3 at male piRNA loci drives spermatogenic piRNA transcription and requires SNPC-4.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by ChIP experiments with SNPC-4 depletion in Figure 4.

claim: Loss of snpc-1.3 leads to depletion of male piRNAs.
source: Loss of snpc-1.3 leads to depletion of male piRNAs and defects in male-dependent fertility.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by qPCR and small RNA-seq data in Figure 3.

claim: Loss of snpc-1.3 leads to defects in male-dependent fertility.
source: Loss of snpc-1.3 leads to depletion of male piRNAs and defects in male-dependent fertility.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by fertility assays in Figure 6.

claim: TRA-1 binds to the snpc-1.3 promoter.
source: Furthermore, TRA-1, a master regulator of sex determination, binds to the snpc-1.3 promoter and represses its expression during oogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by ChIP-seq data in Figure 5B.

claim: TRA-1 represses snpc-1.3 expression during oogenesis.
source: Furthermore, TRA-1, a master regulator of sex determination, binds to the snpc-1.3 promoter and represses its expression during oogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNAi and TRA-1 binding site mutation experiments in Figure 5C.

claim: Loss of TRA-1 targeting causes ectopic expression of snpc-1.3 during oogenesis.
source: Loss of TRA-1 targeting causes ectopic expression of snpc-1.3 and male piRNAs during oogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by experiments with TRA-1 binding site mutants in Figure 5C.

claim: Loss of TRA-1 targeting causes ectopic expression of male piRNAs during oogenesis.
source: Loss of TRA-1 targeting causes ectopic expression of snpc-1.3 and male piRNAs during oogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by small RNA-seq in TRA-1 binding site mutants in Figure 5D-E.

claim: Sexually dimorphic regulation of snpc-1.3 expression coordinates male and female piRNA expression during germline development.
source: Thus, sexually dimorphic regulation of snpc-1.3 expression coordinates male and female piRNA expression during germline development.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing the findings about TRA-1 regulation and piRNA expression.

claim: piRNAs play essential roles in silencing repetitive elements to promote fertility in metazoans.
source: Piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) play essential roles in silencing repetitive elements to promote fertility in metazoans.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations to previous literature throughout the introduction.

claim: piRNAs are expressed in a sex-specific manner in worms, flies, and mammals.
source: Studies in worms, flies, and mammals reveal that piRNAs are expressed in a sex-specific manner.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Armisen et al., 2009; Billi et al., 2013; Williams et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2010).

claim: Mutation of any of the three Drosophila Piwi genes results in rampant activation of transposons in the germline.
source: In Drosophila, mutation of any of the three Piwi genes (piwi, aub, ago3) results in rampant activation of transposons in the germline and severe defects in fertility (Brennecke et al., 2007; Harris and Macdonald, 2001; Lin and Spradling, 1997; Vagin et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Mutation of any of the three Drosophila Piwi genes results in severe defects in fertility.
source: In Drosophila, mutation of any of the three Piwi genes (piwi, aub, ago3) results in rampant activation of transposons in the germline and severe defects in fertility (Brennecke et al., 2007; Harris and Macdonald, 2001; Lin and Spradling, 1997; Vagin et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Mutation of the mouse Piwi protein MIWI leads to misregulation of genes involved in germ cell development.
source: In Mus musculus, mutation of the Piwi protein MIWI leads to the misregulation of genes involved in germ cell development, defective gametogenesis, and sterility (Deng and Lin, 2002; Zhang et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Mutation of the mouse Piwi protein MIWI leads to defective gametogenesis and sterility.
source: In Mus musculus, mutation of the Piwi protein MIWI leads to the misregulation of genes involved in germ cell development, defective gametogenesis, and sterility (Deng and Lin, 2002; Zhang et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: C. elegans piRNAs can be inherited across multiple generations.
source: Caenorhabditis elegans piRNAs can be inherited across multiple generations and trigger the transgenerational silencing of foreign elements such as transgenes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Ashe et al., 2012; Buckley et al., 2012; Shirayama et al., 2012).

claim: C. elegans piRNAs trigger the transgenerational silencing of foreign elements such as transgenes.
source: Caenorhabditis elegans piRNAs can be inherited across multiple generations and trigger the transgenerational silencing of foreign elements such as transgenes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Ashe et al., 2012; Buckley et al., 2012; Shirayama et al., 2012).

claim: Disruption of piRNA inheritance in C. elegans results in eventual germline collapse and sterility, known as the germline mortal phenotype.
source: Disruption of this inheritance results in eventual germline collapse and sterility, known as the germline mortal phenotype (Ashe et al., 2012; Buckley et al., 2012; Shirayama et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: piRNAs are essential to preserve germline integrity and ensure reproductive capacity in metazoans.
source: Taken together, piRNAs are essential to preserve germline integrity and ensure the reproductive capacity in metazoans.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the introduction based on the cited evidence from multiple organisms.

claim: Many species show sex-specific expression of piRNAs.
source: Many species show sex-specific expression of piRNAs (Armisen et al., 2009; Billi et al., 2013; Williams et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The identity of maternal, but not paternal, piRNAs in flies is important for fertility of progeny.
source: Demonstrated by hybrid dysgenesis, the identity of maternal, but not paternal, piRNAs in flies is important for fertility of progeny (Brennecke et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The piRNA pathway in mammals appears to be dispensable for female fertility.
source: In contrast, the piRNA pathway in mammals appears to be dispensable for female fertility (Carmell et al., 2007; Murchison et al., 2007), but distinct subsets of piRNAs are required for specific stages of spermatogenesis (Aravin et al., 2003; Aravin et al., 2006; Carmell et al., 2007; Di Giacomo et al., 2013; Gainetdinov et al., 2018; Girard et al., 2006; Grivna et al., 2006; Kuramochi-Miyagawa et al., 2008; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Distinct subsets of piRNAs are required for specific stages of spermatogenesis in mammals.
source: In contrast, the piRNA pathway in mammals appears to be dispensable for female fertility (Carmell et al., 2007; Murchison et al., 2007), but distinct subsets of piRNAs are required for specific stages of spermatogenesis (Aravin et al., 2003; Aravin et al., 2006; Carmell et al., 2007; Di Giacomo et al., 2013; Gainetdinov et al., 2018; Girard et al., 2006; Grivna et al., 2006; Kuramochi-Miyagawa et al., 2008; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Most piRNAs in C. elegans are uniquely enriched in either the male or female germline.
source: In worms, most piRNAs are uniquely enriched in either the male or female germline (Billi et al., 2013; Kato et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In Drosophila germline, piRNA clusters are found within pericentromeric or telomeric heterochromatin enriched for H3K9me3 histone modifications.
source: In the Drosophila germline, piRNA clusters are found within pericentromeric or telomeric heterochromatin enriched for H3K9me3 histone modifications.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Andersen et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2016; Klattenhoff et al., 2009; Mohn et al., 2014; Pane et al., 2011).

claim: The HP1 homolog Rhino binds to H3K9me3 within most piRNA clusters in Drosophila.
source: The HP1 homolog Rhino binds to H3K9me3 within most of these piRNA clusters and recruits Moonshiner, a paralog of the basal transcription factor TFIIA, which, in turn, recruits RNA polymerase II (Pol II) to enable transcription within heterochromatin (Andersen et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2016; Klattenhoff et al., 2009; Mohn et al., 2014; Pane et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Rhino recruits Moonshiner, a paralog of the basal transcription factor TFIIA, in Drosophila piRNA biogenesis.
source: The HP1 homolog Rhino binds to H3K9me3 within most of these piRNA clusters and recruits Moonshiner, a paralog of the basal transcription factor TFIIA, which, in turn, recruits RNA polymerase II (Pol II) to enable transcription within heterochromatin (Andersen et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2016; Klattenhoff et al., 2009; Mohn et al., 2014; Pane et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Moonshiner recruits RNA polymerase II to enable transcription within heterochromatin in Drosophila.
source: The HP1 homolog Rhino binds to H3K9me3 within most of these piRNA clusters and recruits Moonshiner, a paralog of the basal transcription factor TFIIA, which, in turn, recruits RNA polymerase II (Pol II) to enable transcription within heterochromatin (Andersen et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2016; Klattenhoff et al., 2009; Mohn et al., 2014; Pane et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Two waves of piRNA expression occur in mouse testes: pre-pachytene piRNAs and pachytene piRNAs.
source: Two waves of piRNA expression occur in mouse testes: pre-pachytene piRNAs are expressed in early spermatogenesis and silence transposons, whereas pachytene piRNAs are expressed in the later stages of meiosis and have unknown functions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Li et al., 2013).

claim: Pre-pachytene piRNAs are expressed in early spermatogenesis and silence transposons in mice.
source: Two waves of piRNA expression occur in mouse testes: pre-pachytene piRNAs are expressed in early spermatogenesis and silence transposons, whereas pachytene piRNAs are expressed in the later stages of meiosis and have unknown functions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Li et al., 2013).

claim: Pachytene piRNAs are expressed in the later stages of meiosis and have unknown functions in mice.
source: Two waves of piRNA expression occur in mouse testes: pre-pachytene piRNAs are expressed in early spermatogenesis and silence transposons, whereas pachytene piRNAs are expressed in the later stages of meiosis and have unknown functions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Li et al., 2013).

claim: Pachytene piRNAs require the transcription factor A-MYB and RNA Pol II in mice.
source: While the mechanisms of pre-pachytene piRNA transcription remain elusive, pachytene piRNAs require the transcription factor A-MYB, along with RNA Pol II (Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SNPC-4 is essential for the expression of piRNAs in the C. elegans germline.
source: In C. elegans, SNPC-4 is essential for the expression of piRNAs in the germline (Kasper et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SNPC-4 is the single C. elegans ortholog of mammalian SNAPC4.
source: SNPC-4 is the single C. elegans ortholog of mammalian SNAPC4, the largest DNA binding subunit of the small nuclear RNA (snRNA) activating protein complex (SNAPc).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Henry et al., 1995; Jawdekar and Henry, 2008; Ma and Hernandez, 2002; Su et al., 1997; Wong et al., 1998; Yoon et al., 1995).

claim: A complex of SNAPC4, SNAPC1, and SNAPC3 binds to the proximal sequence element (PSE) of snRNA loci to promote their transcription.
source: A complex of SNAPC4, SNAPC1, and SNAPC3 binds to the proximal sequence element (PSE) of snRNA loci to promote their transcription (Henry et al., 1995; Jawdekar and Henry, 2008; Ma and Hernandez, 2002; Su et al., 1997; Wong et al., 1998; Yoon et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SNPC-4 occupies transcription start sites of other classes of noncoding RNAs across various C. elegans tissue types and developmental stages.
source: SNPC-4 occupies transcription start sites of other classes of noncoding RNAs across various C. elegans tissue types and developmental stages (Kasper et al., 2014; Weng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: piRNA biogenesis factors PRDE-1, TOFU-4, and TOFU-5 are expressed in germ cell nuclei and interact with SNPC-4 at clusters of piRNA loci.
source: Furthermore, piRNA biogenesis factors PRDE-1, TOFU-4, and TOFU-5 are expressed in germ cell nuclei and interact with SNPC-4 at clusters of piRNA loci (Goh et al., 2014; Kasper et al., 2014; Weick et al., 2014; Weng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SNPC-4 has been co-opted by germline-specific factors to transcribe piRNAs.
source: These data suggest that SNPC-4 has been co-opted by germline-specific factors to transcribe piRNAs.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the introduction based on the cited evidence.

claim: The vast majority of the ~15,000 piRNAs in C. elegans are encoded within two large megabase genomic clusters on chromosome IV.
source: The vast majority of the ~15,000 piRNAs in C. elegans are encoded within two large megabase genomic clusters on chromosome IV (Das et al., 2008; Ruby et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Each piRNA locus in C. elegans encodes a discrete transcriptional unit that is individually transcribed as a short precursor by Pol II.
source: Each piRNA locus encodes a discrete transcriptional unit that is individually transcribed as a short precursor by Pol II (Gu et al., 2012; Cecere et al., 2012; Billi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Processing of piRNA precursors yields mature piRNAs that are typically 21 nucleotides in length.
source: Processing of precursors yields mature piRNAs that are typically 21 nucleotides (nt) in length and strongly enriched for a 5′ uracil (referred to as 21U-RNAs).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge about C. elegans piRNAs.

claim: Mature piRNAs in C. elegans are strongly enriched for a 5′ uracil.
source: Processing of precursors yields mature piRNAs that are typically 21 nucleotides (nt) in length and strongly enriched for a 5′ uracil (referred to as 21U-RNAs).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge about C. elegans piRNAs.

claim: Transcription of C. elegans piRNAs requires a conserved eight nt core motif (NNGTTTCA) within their promoters.
source: Transcription of these piRNAs requires a conserved eight nt core motif (NNGTTTCA) within their promoters (Billi et al., 2013; Cecere et al., 2012; Ruby et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: piRNAs enriched during spermatogenesis are associated with a cytosine at the 5′ most position of the core motif (CNGTTTCA).
source: piRNAs enriched during spermatogenesis are associated with a cytosine at the 5′ most position of the core motif (CNGTTTCA); mutation of cytosine to adenine at this position results in ectopic expression of normally male-enriched piRNAs during oogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation (Billi et al., 2013).

claim: Mutation of cytosine to adenine at the 5′ position of the core motif results in ectopic expression of normally male-enriched piRNAs during oogenesis.
source: piRNAs enriched during spermatogenesis are associated with a cytosine at the 5′ most position of the core motif (CNGTTTCA); mutation of cytosine to adenine at this position results in ectopic expression of normally male-enriched piRNAs during oogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation (Billi et al., 2013).

claim: Genomic loci expressing piRNAs enriched in the female germline show no discernable nucleotide bias at the 5′ position of the core motif.
source: In contrast, genomic loci expressing piRNAs enriched in the female germline show no discernable nucleotide bias at the 5′ position (Billi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SNPC-4 is required for piRNA biogenesis in both the male and female germline.
source: We hypothesized that SNPC-4 is required for piRNA biogenesis in both the male and female germline.
evidence: This hypothesis is stated and then tested with auxin-inducible degradation experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Worms depleted of SNPC-4 showed decreased expression of both spermatogenesis- and oogenesis-enriched piRNAs.
source: Worms depleted of SNPC-4 showed decreased expression of both spermatogenesis- and oogenesis-enriched piRNAs during spermatogenesis and oogenesis time points, respectively (Figure 1A), confirming that SNPC-4 is a core piRNA transcription factor required for all piRNA expression.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: SNPC-4 is a core piRNA transcription factor required for all piRNA expression.
source: Worms depleted of SNPC-4 showed decreased expression of both spermatogenesis- and oogenesis-enriched piRNAs during spermatogenesis and oogenesis time points, respectively (Figure 1A), confirming that SNPC-4 is a core piRNA transcription factor required for all piRNA expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the depletion experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: PRDE-1 and TOFU-5 co-purified with SNPC-4::3xFlag in both him-8(-) and fem-1(-) mutants.
source: PRDE-1 and TOFU-5 co-purified with SNPC-4::3xFlag in both him-8(-) and fem-1(-) mutants, suggesting that these known piRNA biogenesis factors exist as a complex in both male and female germlines (Figure 1B,C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: PRDE-1 and TOFU-5 exist as a complex with SNPC-4 in both male and female germlines.
source: PRDE-1 and TOFU-5 co-purified with SNPC-4::3xFlag in both him-8(-) and fem-1(-) mutants, suggesting that these known piRNA biogenesis factors exist as a complex in both male and female germlines (Figure 1B,C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the co-purification data.

claim: The C. elegans genome encodes four homologs of human SNAPC1.
source: While a single worm ortholog, SNPC-4, exists for human SNAPC4, the C. elegans genome encodes four homologs of human SNAPC1 (worm SNPC-1.1, -1.2, -1.3, and -1.5) and four homologs of human SNAPC3 (worm SNPC-3.1, -3.2, -3.3, and -3.4, Figure 1B; Li et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B, with a supporting citation.

claim: The C. elegans genome encodes four homologs of human SNAPC3.
source: While a single worm ortholog, SNPC-4, exists for human SNAPC4, the C. elegans genome encodes four homologs of human SNAPC1 (worm SNPC-1.1, -1.2, -1.3, and -1.5) and four homologs of human SNAPC3 (worm SNPC-3.1, -3.2, -3.3, and -3.4, Figure 1B; Li et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B, with a supporting citation.

claim: Six of the eight C. elegans homologs of SNAPC1 and SNAPC3 co-purified with SNPC-4::3xFlag from both him-8(-) and fem-1(-) genetic backgrounds.
source: From our mass spectrometry analysis, six of the eight C. elegans homologs of SNAPC1 and SNAPC3 co-purified with SNPC-4::3xFlag from both him-8(-) and fem-1(-) genetic backgrounds (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: SNPC-4 interacts with both snRNA and piRNA transcriptional machinery.
source: These results revealed that SNPC-4 interacts with both snRNA and piRNA transcriptional machinery.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the mass spectrometry data.

claim: SNPC-1.3 co-purified with SNPC-4::3xFlag from him-8(-), but not fem-1(-) mutants.
source: We also identified proteins that co-purified with SNPC-4::3xFlag from him-8(-), but not fem-1(-) mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: SNPC-4::3xFlag and SNPC-1.3:Ollas interacted robustly during spermatogenesis.
source: In agreement with the mass spectrometry data, SNPC-4::3xFlag and SNPC-1.3:Ollas interacted robustly during spermatogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The interaction between SNPC-4::3xFlag and SNPC-1.3:Ollas was detectable at a much lower level during oogenesis.
source: The interaction was detectable at a much lower level during oogenesis (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: SNPC-1.3 forms a complex with the piRNA biogenesis factor SNPC-4.
source: The reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation of SNPC-1.3::3xFlag followed by western blotting for SNPC-4::Ollas confirmed this biochemical interaction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H), suggesting that SNPC-1.3 forms a complex with the previously characterized piRNA biogenesis factor SNPC-4.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by reciprocal co-IP data.

claim: Knockdown of glp-1 mRNA markedly reduced both snpc-1.3 and snpc-4 mRNAs.
source: Knockdown of glp-1 mRNA markedly reduced both snpc-1.3 and snpc-4 mRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: SNPC-1.3::3xFlag protein expression was reduced in a glp-4 temperature-sensitive mutant.
source: SNPC-1.3::3xFlag protein expression was also reduced in a glp-4 temperature-sensitive mutant, which fails to develop fully expanded germlines at 25°C (Beanan and Strome, 1992), suggesting that SNPC-1.3 is predominantly expressed in the germline (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: SNPC-1.3 is predominantly expressed in the germline.
source: SNPC-1.3::3xFlag protein expression was also reduced in a glp-4 temperature-sensitive mutant, which fails to develop fully expanded germlines at 25°C (Beanan and Strome, 1992), suggesting that SNPC-1.3 is predominantly expressed in the germline (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the glp-4 mutant data.

claim: The expression of snpc-1.3 mRNA was greatly enriched in him-8(-) males relative to fem-1(-) females.
source: The expression of snpc-1.3 mRNA was greatly enriched in him-8(-) relative to fem-1(-), while snpc-4 mRNA did not show any differential expression.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: snpc-4 mRNA did not show differential expression between him-8(-) males and fem-1(-) females.
source: The expression of snpc-1.3 mRNA was greatly enriched in him-8(-) relative to fem-1(-), while snpc-4 mRNA did not show any differential expression.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: SNPC-1.3::3xFlag protein was highly enriched in males as compared to females.
source: At the protein level, SNPC-1.3::3xFlag was also highly enriched in males as compared to females by western blotting (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: SNPC-4 localizes to one or two foci in each germline nuclei.
source: SNPC-4, along with other piRNA factors, such as PRDE-1, localize to one or two foci in each germline nuclei (Kasper et al., 2014; Weick et al., 2014; Weng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: In the male germline, SNPC-1.3::Ollas colocalized with SNPC-4::3xFlag in the same nuclear foci.
source: In the male germline, SNPC-1.3::Ollas colocalized with SNPC-4::3xFlag in the same nuclear foci (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: No SNPC-1.3::Ollas signal was detected above background in hermaphrodites.
source: In contrast, no SNPC-1.3::Ollas signal was detected above background in hermaphrodites (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: SNPC-1.3 co-localizes with SNPC-4 specifically in the male germline.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that SNPC-1.3 co-localizes with SNPC-4 specifically in the male germline.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the immunofluorescence data.

claim: Levels of male piRNAs were dramatically reduced in him-8(-); snpc-1.3(-) males.
source: Levels of male piRNAs were dramatically reduced in snpc-1.3(-) hermaphrodites during spermatogenesis and in him-8(-); snpc-1.3(-) males, whereas female piRNAs were largely unaltered in snpc-1.3(-) adult hermaphrodites and in fem-1(-); snpc-1.3(-) females (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Female piRNAs were largely unaltered in snpc-1.3(-) adult hermaphrodites.
source: Levels of male piRNAs were dramatically reduced in snpc-1.3(-) hermaphrodites during spermatogenesis and in him-8(-); snpc-1.3(-) males, whereas female piRNAs were largely unaltered in snpc-1.3(-) adult hermaphrodites and in fem-1(-); snpc-1.3(-) females (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Female piRNAs were largely unaltered in fem-1(-); snpc-1.3(-) females.
source: Levels of male piRNAs were dramatically reduced in snpc-1.3(-) hermaphrodites during spermatogenesis and in him-8(-); snpc-1.3(-) males, whereas female piRNAs were largely unaltered in snpc-1.3(-) adult hermaphrodites and in fem-1(-); snpc-1.3(-) females (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Female piRNAs were moderately upregulated by at least twofold in snpc-1.3(-) mutants undergoing spermatogenesis.
source: Unexpectedly, female piRNAs were also moderately upregulated by at least twofold in snpc-1.3(-) mutants undergoing spermatogenesis and in him-8(-); snpc-1.3(-) males.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Female piRNAs were moderately upregulated by at least twofold in him-8(-); snpc-1.3(-) males.
source: Unexpectedly, female piRNAs were also moderately upregulated by at least twofold in snpc-1.3(-) mutants undergoing spermatogenesis and in him-8(-); snpc-1.3(-) males.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: SNPC-1.3 suppresses the expression of female piRNAs in the male germline, possibly by preferentially recruiting core factors such as SNPC-4 to male piRNA loci.
source: These findings suggest that, in addition to activating male piRNAs, SNPC-1.3 suppresses the expression of female piRNAs in the male germline, possibly by preferentially recruiting core factors such as SNPC-4 to male piRNA loci.
